item.content:encoded: Personally, I like this one for its simplicity. Not a lot of background, but what we do get is intriguing. We don't know its origin, only that it was found alongside a quote by a poet remembered for writing on the virtues of man while remaining aware of the absurdity of human existence. SCPs like this one always seem like "easter eggs" hidden by [powers/deities/beings], and seem to me to seamlessly alternate between spooky and absurd (absurd in the sense that LIFE is frequently quite absurd, and one is left to make one's own assumptions once one realizes the gods are just as crazy as we are sometimes).

These questions are important for me to become invested in this SCP.

item.content:encoded:
I upvoted this. My only problem with it is that the fact that it kills you isn't made really clear, just that it stops you from moving. This could mean that it vibrates at a specific wavelength to shatter your bones or whatever, I didn't take it killing you for granted. Also, not really Keter. Hell this thing borders on safe if one could come up with a material that it couldn't abrade away.

Re: vacuum sealing the chamber - this sounds like a really bad idea. This would put the interior under great pressure and if there was ever a problem in the facility, like a containment breach, could easily result in a room blowout which could have unpredictable results on the SCP. The only reason to employ a vacuum is if it did something to inhibit the SCP's movements or something but we have no reason to believe it would. Since nobody should be in the chamber anyway, unless repairing it, then there's no reason to have a room that could explode if maintenance fails or other SCP's get involved.

item.content:encoded:
It really should be Euclid. I don't see the justification for Keter. It requires some maintenance, so I'd say it doesn't pass the locked box test because it can't just be "forgotten", but as others have mentioned, make containment a vacuum and there are no sounds to trigger it anyway.

It's restricted by line of sight, as well. From the description, it sounds like I could walk up to the containment box and pound away at it, but without being in line of sight of 339, it wouldn't do anything because there's no movement for it to "see" in that situation.

Overall, it just doesn't do it for me. Don't think anything could change that would make me like it, either.

I know it actively 'neutralizes' anything that makes noise near it, but that would only stop anything it can reach. maybe some test logs concerning maximum range and penetration capabilities (through armor or maybe a concrete wall, etc), as well as how many, if there is a limit, on how many noises it can neutralize at once. what happens if this thing gets loose? XK class end-of-the-world scenario or something? I like this article, but it feels a little barren compared to most Keter level objects. My favorite articles are the Keters that go really in depth about what could happen, and I'd like to see this become one of them.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
SCP-339 constantly produces an aerosolized corrosive compound which is so far unidentifiable due to the rate of molecular breakdown. This gradually degrades any container SCP-339 is placed into, necessitating a double-box approach to containment, consisting of a sound-proofed room and sound-proofed box. The box should be constructed of a specialized zinc-cadmium alloy (339-CA08T), which has proven to be the most resistant against SCP-339's corrosion. This box must be replaced monthly to maintain containment. All work must be done in absolute silence.

Not only does this make me dislike the article immensely, but it belongs in the containment procedures section.
